questions.knowledge_point: Using a Matrix That Represents a Rotation of 90 Degrees
questions.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at  $(-2,-1),(1,3),(2,-3).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${270}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(-3,1)$
- $(-3,2)$
- $(1,-2)$
questions.worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${270}^{∘}$ is the same as counterclockwise rotation by an angle of ${90}^{∘}.$ It's given by the matrix

$$
R[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(1,-2),(-3,1),(3,2).$

So, the correct answer is "I and III only."

Consider the vector $v$ shown above. Find the vector $Av$ given that 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis ${i,j}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors. Computing the images of ${i,j}$ under $A$, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =Ai=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j \\ {j}^{′} & =Aj=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14003089/assets/77936c4115b37d79ae301a93b218ecd23114ae4ad42d8298b8f058c1f50e82a2.png)

So, the matrix represents a rotation of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians **clockwise** about the origin.

Therefore, in order to find $Av$, we need to rotate $v$ **clockwise** by an angle of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians, as shown below.

questions.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at  $(5,-1),(2,0),(-2,-1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation ${R}_{-\pi /2}$ by an angle of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians about the origin?

- $(-1,-5)$
- $(0,2)$
- $(-1,-2)$
questions.worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-\pi /2}$ by an angle of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians is the same as counterclockwise rotation by an angle of $\frac{3\pi }{2}.$ It's given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-\pi /2},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-\pi /2}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -1 \\ -5 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-1,-5),(0,-2),(-1,2).$

So, the correct answer is "I only."
